title: Road Rage Shooter Gets the Surprise of His Life
description:
This video is sponsored by SafetyVid.org which uses a network of 10,000 cameras to automatically capture video of highway crashes. Yes, you can get video of YOUR crash today at SafetyVid.org.
 
Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

THIS DISEASE HITS KIDS HARD - WE'LL MATCH YOUR DONATION :
Angelman Syndrome is a rare disease most commonly diagnosed in young children. Donate today and we'll match it! -- https://www.angelman.org
Send proof of donation to mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com  

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

ABOUT MIDWEST SAFETY:
Midwest Safety works to promote transparency in government while providing educational, informative and local news coverage to empower the public with knowledge of the inner workings of the Criminal Justice System.

The answers list that they found a large AK-47-style black BB rifle on the backseat floor of Travis' car, identified as a Crosman Full Auto AK-1-4.5-millimeter BB Air Rifle, which is capable of firing 1,400 rounds per minute, or about 23 per second. Travis has an extensive criminal history extending back to 2006, with previous charges for possession of cocaine, possession of THC, bail jumping, and operating a vehicle while suspended. For this case, Travis was assigned. a $75,000 cash bond after his arrest. While awaiting trial, his defense twice requested a bond reduction, but the court denied both motions. He also caught a charge for disorderly conduct while in jail. Travis faced charges for one count of first degree recklessly endangering safety with a modifier for use of a dangerous weapon, one count of possession of THC as a second offense, and one count of criminal damage to property, with a modifier for use of a dangerous weapon. Over six months after his arrest, Travis agreed to a no-contest plea deal and was sentenced to one year and 10 months in state prison and five years of probation for one count of first-degree recklessly endangering safety. Conditions include anger management assessments, counseling if recommended, strict alcohol and drug sobriety, and a ban on owning firearms, which additionally included BB guns specifically. All other charges were dismissed. The victim requested nearly $20,000 in restitution for damages, citing losses from her vehicle's decreased value, inability to perform for her delivery job due to a newfound fear of driving and mental health impacts, requiring several counseling sessions. Quotes from documents note that she became paranoid to drive on the highway and that the event had an almost immeasurable impact on her. After legal discussions, the court granted a reduced restitution of just over $4,000. Having been sentenced in August of 2022, Travis should be out of prison at this point and on probation. However, he is still fighting the court's decision on this case. He submitted an appeal in hopes to reverse the charges and reduce the restitution amount. The final decision for that outcome is yet to be determined.
